pricing_why_toggle: Why it's set up this way
pricing_why: This isn't the price of development — that's already paid for: you're deploying a ready system, not commissioning a new one. Features are identical on every tier — nothing is stripped from the lowest one. A crew here means a working group on site with one foreman login, not a fixed set of people: the tier is based on how many crews are active at once. The price grows with that number because of support volume, not the server, and every tier is fixed by contract.
pricing_why_mobile: Development is already paid for — the base is low. Features are identical on every tier, nothing stripped out. A crew means a working group on site, not a fixed set of people. Price grows with crew count because of support volume, not the server.
pricing_time_title: What happens in the launch month
pricing_time: The first week is the intense one: we check rates, pull data out of Excel and walk the foreman through the first sites — on your side that's a few hours. After that, about an hour a week. By the end of the month you're looking at your own sites and payouts in the system, not at a presentation.
pricing_time_mobile: The first week is intense — checking rates, migrating data, walking the foreman through the sites. After that, about an hour a week.

faq_sub: Real questions business owners ask us before their first step.
faq_a1: The system doesn't make money on its own — it shows you where you're losing it: rates below average, unbilled extra work, missing receipts. The payback maths is simple: what one missed piece of extra work or one underpriced rate costs you, and how many of those you have a month. Call us — we'll run the numbers on your sites, not in general.
faq_a2: Objecty as-is — €1,500 launch (about a month of working together: your rates, migration from Excel, training foremen), then from €150/month. The full table is in "How much this costs" above; what fits you specifically, we'll tell you in five minutes on the phone.
faq_q3: Do we need to have systems or vendors already selected?
faq_a3: No. We can start from scratch — picking the right tools, improving what you've got, or just working out where to begin. We're not tied to any vendor, so the advice is about what fits your situation.
faq_q4: Can you work with our existing systems and tools?
faq_a4: Yes — and usually that's the whole point. Most jobs are about connecting or improving what you already run, not ripping it out and starting over. Integrations on top of existing systems are our main thing.
faq_q6: What if it turns out nothing needs to be automated?
faq_a6: Then we'll say so. If a small process change or a spreadsheet template fixes it, that's what you'll hear from us. We're not here to build things you don't actually need.
faq_q7: What kinds of businesses do you work with?
faq_a7: We work best with companies where the work is done by people on-site, not in an office: one crew or several, and tracking still runs on Excel, WhatsApp and the owner's memory. That's construction and renovation, fit-out and installation, service calls, cleaning and grounds maintenance — they all have the same problem: figuring out who did what, where, and what they're owed for it. We also work with warehouses, logistics and small manufacturing.
faq_q8: Who supports the system after launch?
faq_a8: Support is included in the launch and the subscription: server, updates, response during business hours. An outage over a weekend when the month is closing is a working day too, not a reason to wait until Monday.
faq_a9: The main thing is that the data is yours: sites, crews, rates and payouts can be exported any time without our involvement, and you have access from day one. We deliberately picked the most ordinary technologies so that any developer can maintain the system, not just us. The source code stays with us; if getting it matters to you, that goes into the contract before work starts.
